title: Mixtures and Water Resources
seo_title: Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology: Mixtures and Water Resources Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology: Mixtures and water resources; processes to purify water
standard_text: Water in rivers and dams can be polluted with solids, chemicals and germs. Water is purified by settling, sieving, filtering, adding chemicals and boiling. Clean water is a scarce resource in South Africa and must be saved. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 6, Matter and Materials: Mixtures and water resources; processes to purify water)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): water resources, pollution, settling, sieving, filtering, boiling and saving water. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Filtering removes solids; boiling kills germs.
key_sub: Water is scarce, so we must save it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water from a river or dam may contain sand, leaves, chemicals and germs. It is purified in steps: settling (heavy solids sink), sieving and filtering (remove small solids), adding chemicals such as chlorine (kills germs) and boiling (kills germs at home).

South Africa is a dry country with limited fresh water. We must not pollute rivers and should save water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water and collect rainwater.

Example

Which step kills germs in water at home?

Heat it

Answer: boiling

Example

Muddy water is poured through a coffee filter. What is removed?

What is too big for the holes?

Answer: the mud (solids)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clear water is always safe to drink.
  • Thinking filtering removes germs and dissolved salts.
  • Thinking water will never run out.

faq.q: Why is chlorine added to tap water?
faq.a: It kills germs that cause diseases such as cholera.

items.q: Which method is best for separating steel cans and aluminium cans at a recycling plant?
items.e: Steel is attracted to a magnet; aluminium is not.

items.q: Which method is best for separating sugar from sugar solution?
items.e: Heat gently: the solvent evaporates and the solute remains.

items.q: Which method is best for separating chalk powder and water?
items.e: Chalk is insoluble.

items.q: What is a solute?
c: the substance that does the dissolving
a solid that does not dissolve
items.e: Sugar is the solute in sugar water.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sea water (to get the salt)?
items.e: Use evaporating because salt is dissolved in sea water.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate salt and water?
items.e: Use evaporating because salt is dissolved, so the water must evaporate.

items.q: Which method is best for separating pure water from sea water?
items.e: Water boils, turns into vapour and is condensed back into a liquid.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate the colours in a food colouring?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate paperclips and marbles?
items.e: Use using a magnet because steel paperclips are magnetic; glass marbles are not.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by filtration?
c: the different dyes in a black ink
copper sulfate crystals from copper sulfate solution
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate tea leaves from tea?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which method is best for separating tea leaves and tea?
items.e: The tea leaves are the residue.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate rice and flour?
items.e: Use sieving because the flour is fine enough to pass through.

items.q: Which method is best for separating the colourings in a sweet?
items.e: Each colouring travels at its own rate.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate the different dyes in a black ink?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by chromatography?
c: the colours in a food colouring
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sugar and water?
items.e: Use evaporating because sugar is dissolved.

items.q: Which method is best for separating sand and water?
items.e: Sand is insoluble, so it stays on the filter paper.

items.q: Which method is best for separating the dyes in a black marker ink?
items.e: The dyes move different distances up the paper.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate pure water from sea water?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Kgomotso mixes 20 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, sand and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by filtering (after sieving, using a magnet and adding water)?
items.e: The insoluble solid is caught in the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains pebbles, salt and sand. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: Nadia mixes 10 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Which step comes last?
c: Evaporate the water to get the salt back.
Use a magnet to remove the iron filings.
Add water and stir so the salt dissolves.
items.e: Evaporating leaves the dissolved salt behind at the end.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, salt and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by a sieve?
items.e: Only the big pieces are too large to pass through.

items.q: A dry mixture contains chalk powder, gravel and sugar. Which part is separated out by a sieve?
items.e: Only the big pieces are too large to pass through.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Which step is a good first step?
c: Evaporate the water to get the salt back.
Use a magnet to remove the iron filings.
Add water and stir so the salt dissolves.
items.e: Take out the magnetic iron first, while everything is dry.

items.q: Liam dissolves 5 g of salt in 150 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Daniel dissolves 10 g of salt in 50 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Lungile mixes 8 g of sand with 50 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Bongani dissolves 12 g of salt in 100 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Why is water added and stirred before filtering?
c: so the salt dissolves and passes through the filter, leaving the sand
items.e: Only the dissolved salt goes through the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, iron filings and sugar. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, salt and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A dry mixture contains gravel, sand and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, steel paperclips and sugar. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: Aisha mixes 25 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Chloe mixes 5 g of sand with 50 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Which is a source of water pollution?
c: fertiliser and manure washing off farm fields
items.e: Runoff carries nutrients and chemicals.

items.q: What is a point source of pollution?
c: pollution from a whole city's roads
pollution from one clear place, like a factory pipe
items.e: Non-point sources come from many places.

items.q: Which household product is safest for the water system?
c: a drain cleaner poured down the sink every day
motor oil poured on the driveway
old medicine flushed down the toilet
items.e: Choose products that break down safely.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by smoke from a ship's engine at sea?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: What is desalination?
c: removing salt from seawater to make fresh water
items.e: It uses a lot of energy.

items.q: Why should you never pour paint or oil down a storm drain?
c: It makes the drain work better.
Storm drains usually flow straight to rivers and lakes without treatment.
items.e: Many drains are marked 'Drains to the lake.'

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by chemicals from a factory poured into a river?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: What is frost wedging?
c: Water freezes in cracks, expands and breaks rock apart.
items.e: Physical weathering.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by detergent washed into a drain?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: Kyle's class studies this problem: “Fertilizer runs off farms into a river.” Which solution would best reduce the impact?
c: rain gardens and permeable pavement that soak up runoff
planting grass buffer strips along the river and using less fertiliser
keeping protected green spaces and wildlife corridors
reusable bags and bans on single-use plastic
items.e: A good solution targets the cause of the impact.

items.q: What does a water treatment plant do?
c: removes particles and germs to make water safe to drink
items.e: Steps include filtering and disinfecting.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by old batteries thrown into the soil?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.

items.q: Why are wetlands important to water systems?
c: They filter pollutants, store floodwater and recharge groundwater.
items.e: Protecting wetlands protects water.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by burning forests that cause haze?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Kyle observes: “Rainwater carries oil and rubbish from car parks into streams.” What impact can this have?
c: warmer water with less oxygen for fish
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Why do some industries reuse cooling water?
c: to save water and reduce thermal pollution
to make water hotter for rivers
items.e: Recycling water saves resources.

items.q: Which test result suggests water has a lot of pollution from fertiliser?
c: high levels of nitrates and phosphates
items.e: Nutrients feed algae blooms.

items.q: Sarah observes: “Fertilizer runs off farms into a river.” What impact can this have?
c: animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: What is permeability?
c: how easily water can flow through a material
items.e: Connected pores.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by honking horns in heavy traffic?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: What are clouds made of?
c: tiny droplets of water (or ice crystals)
items.e: Vapour condenses into droplets.

items.q: Where is most of Earth's water?
items.e: About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water.

items.q: Why does warm water hold less life in a lake?
c: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen.
items.e: Thermal pollution lowers oxygen.

items.q: Why does a cold drink can get wet on the outside?
c: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface.
items.e: Condensation.

items.q: How do permeable pavers help water systems?
c: They add salt to the water.
They let rainwater soak into the ground instead of running off.
items.e: More infiltration recharges groundwater.

items.q: Does the water cycle make new water?
c: No. The same water moves round and round.
items.e: The water on Earth is reused.

items.q: What is one way to reduce farm runoff?
c: leave strips of plants (buffers) along streams
remove all trees by the stream
plough right up to the stream
items.e: Plants trap soil and nutrients.

items.q: Why do towns have water restrictions during a drought?
c: There is little rain, so the stored water must last longer.
items.e: Saving water helps everyone.

items.q: Which of these causes noise pollution?
c: exhaust fumes from cars and buses
items.e: Aircraft taking off near homes leads to noise pollution.

items.q: What is a low-flow showerhead?
c: a showerhead that uses less water per minute
items.e: It saves water and the energy to heat it.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
c: paint washed into a monsoon drain
loud music played near a nature reserve
items.e: Paint washed into a monsoon drain leads to water pollution.

items.q: What happens to water vapour when it cools?
items.e: Cooling causes condensation.

items.q: Which indicator suggests a stream is healthy?
c: lots of foam and a bad smell
many mayfly and stonefly larvae living in it
items.e: Some insects need clean water.

items.q: What is precipitation?
c: water falling from clouds as rain, sleet, snow or hail
items.e: It falls.

items.q: What is water vapour?
items.e: We cannot see it.

items.q: Which part of the water cycle happens when a puddle dries up?
items.e: Liquid to gas.

items.q: What is transpiration?
c: water leaving plant leaves as water vapour
items.e: Trees add lots of water vapour to the air.

items.q: Which of these causes air pollution?
c: loud music played near a nature reserve
items.e: Burning rubbish in the open leads to air pollution.

items.q: How does road salt affect water systems?
c: It washes into streams and groundwater and can harm plants and animals.
It only stays on the road.
items.e: Use only as much salt as needed.

items.q: What does a wastewater treatment plant do?
c: makes drinking water from the ocean
cleans used water from homes before it returns to lakes and rivers
items.e: Sewage must be treated.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: leaving the tap running while soaping hands
using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car
watering plants with water used to wash rice
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: turning off the tap while brushing teeth
washing clothes only when there is a full load
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Why should old medicines be returned to a pharmacy instead of flushed?
c: Treatment plants cannot remove all medicines, so they end up in lakes.
items.e: Take-back programs protect water.

items.q: Why is it best to water lawns in the early morning?
c: Water is cleaner in the morning.
Less water evaporates before it soaks in.
items.e: Smart watering conserves water.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: watering plants with water used to wash rice
leaving the tap running while soaping hands
thawing frozen food under a running tap
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.
